name: Canadian freelance job boards and freelancer associations
summary: Canada-focused places to find freelance and contract postings (especially writing, editing and communications) and groups that support freelancers.
what_you_do: You browse Canadian job banks and boards for freelance, contract or remote postings and apply directly to the client or employer. Associations such as the Canadian Freelance Guild and the Canadian Freelance Union offer job listings or member supports such as insurance and contract advice.
who_it_may_fit: You write, edit or do communications work and want Canadian clients and freelancer supports.
Postings are aimed at people in Canada, and some are open only to Canadian citizens or permanent residents
No marketplace commission when a client hires you directly

who_it_may_not_fit: You need a high volume of quick gigs or have no portfolio to show yet.
Postings lean towards writing, editing and communications
Membership costs and job-bank access terms weren't checked

Listings on aggregators (Glassdoor, SimplyHired, Workopolis) can be stale, so check posting dates
Freelance or contract status usually means no employee benefits

name: Commission-free freelance portfolio and payments (Contra)
summary: Show a portfolio, find or bring your own clients, and get paid without Contra taking a commission from your earnings.
what_you_do: You build a portfolio profile, apply to opportunities or invite your own clients, and handle proposals, contracts and invoices through Contra. Clients pay through the platform, and you withdraw to a payout method such as PayPal or Payoneer.
who_it_may_fit: You already have, or can find, clients, especially for design or creative work, and want to avoid marketplace commissions.
No commission on freelancer earnings (Contra has been commission-free since 2021)
Handy for invoicing clients you find yourself
Portfolio-centred profiles suit designers and other creatives
Most payouts arrive within minutes (Contra help)
who_it_may_not_fit: You need a platform to bring you steady work, or your clients won't accept platform fees.

Payout fees: 2% to PayPal, or a flat $3 to Payoneer plus Payoneer's own charges
Third-party sources say Contra Pro costs about $29/month and some features need it
It's not mainly a job board, so you still have to find clients
Payout options for Canada weren't confirmed in this check

name: Selling freelance service 'gigs' on Fiverr
summary: List fixed-price service packages ('gigs') that buyers can order directly; Fiverr keeps 20% of each sale.
what_you_do: You create gig listings that describe a specific service, with price tiers and delivery times. Buyers find and order your gig, you deliver the work through Fiverr's order system, and your earnings clear to your balance after a holding period.
who_it_may_fit: You can package a clear, repeatable service and can wait while your gigs build reviews and ranking.
Buyers find you through search instead of you bidding on jobs
Simple flat fee: you keep 80% of each order
Faster 7-day clearance and early payout become available at higher seller levels or with Seller Plus
who_it_may_not_fit: You need quick, predictable income or can't absorb a 20% commission.
Fiverr keeps 20% of every order, including tips
Standard sellers' earnings are held for 14 days after an order completes before you can withdraw
Early payout costs 1% and is limited to Top Rated sellers and Seller Plus Premium members
Buyers also pay a 5.5% service fee (plus $3.50 on orders under $200), which makes your gig cost them more
Fiverr Community posts report sudden drops in gig impressions and accounts disabled after several order cancellations
Canada-specific payout methods and fees weren't confirmed in this check

conditions_notes: Orders depend on how your gigs rank in search. Fiverr Community anecdotes describe sudden impression drops and long gaps with no orders.

fees: 20% commission on every order, tips included. Earnings clear after 14 days (7 days for Seller Plus, Top Rated and Pro). Early payout costs 1%. Withdrawal-method fees vary and weren't confirmed for Canada.
economics_notes: You set your gig prices. No earnings data was checked. You receive 80% of the order value after any discounts.

name: Freelance client work through Upwork
summary: Sell services to clients by sending proposals for projects posted on Upwork's freelance marketplace.
what_you_do: You build a profile, then spend 'Connects' to send proposals to clients' job posts. If hired, you agree hourly or fixed-price terms and deliver the work. Upwork deducts its service fee before you withdraw your earnings to your bank.
who_it_may_fit: You have a skill clients pay for, can write persuasive proposals, and can afford some upfront Connects cost while you build reviews.
Large marketplace where clients post jobs you can bid on
The fee is shown before you send a proposal and stays fixed for that contract
Withdrawals straight to a local bank cost a flat $0.99 USD
Reviews and a track record can lead to repeat clients
who_it_may_not_fit: You need income within days or can't afford to spend money on bids that may not pay off.
Since May 2025 the freelancer service fee varies from 0% to 15% per contract (third-party guides say about 10% is typical)
Proposals cost Connects ($0.15 each), and many jobs need about 6–16 or more; third-party guides say Connects spent on proposals generally aren't refunded
New profiles can be rejected when a skill area is crowded (Upwork Community reports)
Forum posts say new freelancers often spend their Connects and get no interviews
Optional Freelancer Plus costs $19.99/month
Canadian bank fees and currency-conversion costs may apply on top

conditions_notes: Work depends on winning proposals. Forum anecdotes describe new freelancers getting no interviews, and there's no official win-rate data.

fees: Freelancer service fee varies 0–15% per contract and is shown before you propose. Basic accounts pay 5% on direct contracts. Connects cost $0.15 each (minimum 10). Freelancer Plus is optional at $19.99/month. Direct to Local Bank withdrawal costs $0.99 USD, with a $5 USD minimum.
economics_notes: You set your rate or bid. No earnings data was checked in this pass. Take-home pay is after the 0–15% service fee, Connects spending and withdrawal costs.
